title: Joint cohomology comparison for a fixed minimal source complex
statement: Let f:X→S and fi:Xi→S (i in Fin n) be flat proper locally finitely presented, and ui:Xi→X over S, with their structure adjunction units universally isomorphisms. Let L be invertible, k:W→S an immersion, w in W, s=k(w), and assume the source bundle on X_s descends from a finite locally free module on Spec kappa(s). Fix derived localization instances for all schemes and localized open sites. Supply an affine U containing w and trivializations of every Li on Xi×S U. Put E=R(f_W)_*(L_W[0]); supply a strictly perfect connective complex K on the localized module site over U, term isomorphisms K^j≅O_U^{derivedFiberBetti(W,E,j,w)} for every integer j, a derived comparison E|U≅Q(K), and arbitrary linear section bases e0:Gamma(K^0)≅A and e1:Gamma(K^1)≅A^m. Then there exist q≥0 and an A-linear b:A^m→A^q annihilating e1(d_K^0(e0 inverse(a))) for every a in A. For p=ker(A→kappa(w)), there exist an additive equivalence alpha:kappa(p) tensor_A A^m≅H^1(X_s,O) and an additive beta:kappa(p) tensor_A A^q→product_i H^1(Xi_s,O), making beta composed with residue base change of b equal to the family of canonical structure-sheaf cohomology pullbacks composed with alpha. This theorem chooses neither U nor K nor the source bases.

source.place: Tag 0BF2, proof before the joint H-one injectivity argument; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BF2

proof.text: Choose the normalized target models on the given affine. Choose a source fibre trivialization using descent. Apply the chosen geometric-map bridge once to obtain one common source equivalence, compatible target equivalences and one chain map per target. The source term-rank/Betti equalities make its residue differentials zero. Hence its degree-one term identifies with residue homology via the canonical cycle-class map, yielding alpha.

Evaluate the chosen chain maps in degree one. Cycle-class functoriality gives the geometric equality on their residue images. Extend each cycle comparison by a vector-space projection onto cycles; take the product. The chain-map equation and zero target degree-zero differentials prove annihilation.

For each C_i^1 use the strictly perfect retract into the finite free sheaf of rank r_i. Evaluate sections, identify the free sections by SheafOfModules.freeSectionsLinearEquiv, and combine the embeddings of t_i. Enumerate the finite sigma type of all coordinates using Fintype.equivFin to obtain q and b. The individual vanishing equations t_i(d(a))=0 and linearity of the embeddings prove the joint annihilation statement.

Assemble the retract projections into rho:A^q to the product of degree-one section modules. The retract identities give rho composed with b equal to t. Base-change this identity using LinearMap.baseChange_comp and compose with the supplied product residue map gamma. The residue comparison equality proves the required square. Empty index sets and zero source rank require no separate branch.
